instructions: Up to a day ahead, or about 45 minutes before you want to serve it, bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tbsp of the salt.
Meanwhile, cut about half the cauliflower into small florets, about 3/4 inch across, until you have 3 cups. Peel the 2 garlic cloves.
Drain the artichoke hearts, pat them dry with paper towels and chop them. Thinly slice the green onions until you have 1/3 cup. Put the artichokes and green onions in a large bowl.

Put the cauliflower and garlic into the boiling water and cook for about 8 minutes, until a fork slides into the cauliflower easily. Lift them into a blender with a slotted spoon and keep the water boiling.
Fill a bowl with ice water. Drop the spinach into the boiling water, and as soon as it wilts, after a few seconds, lift it out into the ice water.
Drain the spinach and squeeze out as much water as you can, or the dip will be runny. Chop it roughly and add it to the bowl with the artichokes.

Once the cauliflower has cooled for a few minutes, add 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 1/2 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/2 tsp Dijon and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt to the blender. Blend for about a minute, until it's smooth and creamy.
Scrape the cauliflower cream into the bowl and stir until everything is evenly mixed.

Brush an 8 inch cast iron skillet or small baking dish with the rest of the olive oil and spread the dip into it. Shred 3/4 cup of the cheddar and scatter it over the top. If you're making it ahead, cover it and keep it in the fridge.
When you're ready to bake, heat the oven to 450°F. If the dip has been in the fridge, leave it on the counter while the oven heats.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, a few minutes longer if it was in the fridge, until the cheese is browned and the edges are bubbling.
Meanwhile, slice the baguette and put the red pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Serve the dip warm with the baguette slices, with the red pepper flakes on the side.
advance_prep_notes: assemble the dip up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge
method_notes: Every version folds squeezed-dry spinach and chopped artichoke hearts into a creamy, cheesy base and serves it warm. Love and Lemons (the lead) makes the base from boiled cauliflower and garlic blended with Greek yogurt, olive oil and Dijon, tops it with white cheddar and bakes it hot at 450°F. Once Upon a Chef cooks it on the stove as a cheddar and half and half sauce with no baking, and I Wash You Dry stirs cream cheese, mayo, sour cream, parmesan and mozzarella together and bakes it at 375°F. This one follows the lead and moves the chili flakes to the side.
